seo.title: Karmic tail 3 13 10 compatibility: what it means for a couple
seo.description: Karmic tail 3 13 10 compatibility: the Empress, Death and the Wheel of Fortune in a couple's tail, and why the romance ends midway while the union goes on.

title: Karmic tail 3-13-10 in compatibility: the romance that ends in the middle
short: When a couple's tail reads 3-13-10, Death stands in the middle of their shared task, and the first question is always the same: does it mean a break-up? No. This tail tells of a different ending: halfway through a life together the romance ends, and the union stays. The Empress at the entry is what the couple wants together: a home, a garden, a shared harvest, and for all of it to last for ever. Death in the middle is the time when the first form of love is spent and held together only by habit. The Wheel of Fortune in the main task is learning that every season of life has its own love, and not trying to bring back the first summer.

sections.h2: A novella with the wedding exactly in the middle
paragraphs: In 1859 Tolstoy published Family Happiness (Semeynoye schastiye) in The Russian Messenger. The story is told by its heroine, seventeen-year-old Masha. She spends the winter after her mother's death in the old house at Pokrovskoye, and in spring her guardian arrives: Sergey Mikhaylych, a friend of her late father, a man of thirty-six. Tolstoy took the material from his own life: «Then the main, the most serious one… that was Arsenyeva, Valeria… I was almost her fiancé (Family Happiness)», he wrote many years later to Pavel Biryukov. Quotations from the novella follow Louise and Aylmer Maude's translation; where it is loose or silent, the translation is ours.

The novella has nine chapters. Many novels of the time end with a wedding, but Tolstoy puts it in the fifth chapter, exactly in the middle. The second half of the book is about what happens to love once the romance has been written to its end. And the wedding day itself, read closely, begins with a memorial service: «Before dinner we walked to our church, to attend a memorial service for my father».

The shape of the novella matches the tail. First the garden, the lilac, the nightingales and the harvest: The Empress. In the middle the wedding, then a frozen winter and three years in which their relations «seemed to have taken a fixed shape». That is Death. At the end, the same veranda, the same bench, the same sonata, and a conversation about how «each time of life has its own kind of love». That is the Wheel. The last sentence of the novella: «That day ended the romance of our marriage; the old feeling became a precious irrecoverable remembrance; but a new feeling of love for my children and the father of my children laid the foundation of a new life and a quite different happiness».

sections.h2: The Empress at the entry: a garden, a harvest and the words «for ever»
paragraphs: A couple's entry to the task is what the two of them want together: shared wishes, agreements, a common language. The point stands on the line of tasks, so the same wish can turn into resistance. Lisovskaya's key to The Empress is fertility, abundance and growth. Tolstoy shows them as scenes rather than words.

Late May, the veranda, the samovar, cream and cracknels, a nightingale in the lilac. Sergey Mikhaylych says: «I wish I could spend all my life here, sitting in this veranda». Katya answers: «Well, do then!» And he: «That's all very well, but life won't sit still». **The tail's main task is spoken aloud on the very first summer evening**, before any confession: the entry wants to sit like this all its life, and the Wheel already knows that life won't sit still.

The first, unintended confession comes during the harvest. From the garden Masha watches the loaded carts of sheaves creak along the road while the field turns to stubble before her eyes: «as if summer had turned into autumn before my eyes». She thinks of happiness as a harvest that needs somewhere to go: «am I to blame for being happy? And how can I share my happiness?» That same evening, in the fenced cherry garden, she hears Sergey Mikhaylych, sure that nobody can see him, softly say: «Darling Masha!»

The couple's shared dream is set down in his words before the wedding: «A quiet secluded life in the country… then work… then rest, nature, books, music, love for one's neighbor -- such is my idea of happiness». Masha answers: «I have always wished for and loved only this quiet family life». That is The Empress at the entry: a house where there is plenty of everything and everything grows.

The resistance hides in a single word. On summer nights Masha felt «a wish never to leave that room -- a wish that dawn might never come», and she thought «that it might always be like this, that such a feeling is given for nothing». Walking in the moonlit garden she felt «that the whole scene must remain fixed for ever in its beauty». On the morning of her wedding: «Can this new life really be for ever?» Some years later, at a German spa: «Let us go to the country, and for ever». Her husband answers: «as for "for ever", that is a dream». **The minus of this entry is the wish for a garden without seasons.**

The couple's common language grows from the same entry: the two of them talk about themselves as if about other people. On the first evening he opens the music at the adagio of Beethoven's «sonata quasi una fantasia», the Moonlight: a sonata «in the manner of a fantasy». He declares himself through «the story about A and B»: an «old and worn-out» Mr A fell in love with young Miss B and decided to go away. The story, he says, has «two different endings». Masha invents a third — «the third ending is that he did not love her, but hurt her» — and on that word confesses her own love. This is The Empress in the plus: a tale told in the third person helps to tell the truth. The minus shows later: «conversation flowed more easily in the presence of a third person».

The numbers hold their own clue. The Empress at the entry is formed the same way in every such couple: one partner has 21, The World, at the same point of the personal matrix, and the other has 9, The Hermit. The whole world and the lantern of solitude add up to a garden. In the novella both terms are heard in one conversation: «Oh, I should like to go round the world with you» — and straight after: «What about my mother? What about my business?» The Russian word svet means both "the world" and "society". A year later the couple quarrels precisely over svet, society: balls, receptions, a prince. And in the last chapter the husband says: «No, it was not society, my dear». This is our reading, not a rule of Lisovskaya's.

sections.h2: Death in the middle: the romance ends, not the union
paragraphs: The middle of the task is our reading: how the couple travels from the wish of the entry to the main task. In this tail the road runs through Death. Waite describes it as a change of form: «The veil or mask of life is perpetuated in change, transformation and passage from lower to higher». What ends is not life but the mask it has worn until now.

The first small death happens in the church itself. Masha expected a miracle, but «nothing extraordinary, nothing worthy of the Sacrament I had just received, had taken place in myself». The kiss felt strange: «Is this all?» Right afterwards, in the carriage, her fear turns into «a new love still more tender and stronger than the old». This is how the middle works in the plus: the old form ends, and another one grows in its place at once.

Then the minus begins. The mother-in-law's house, where «the whole household went like a clock»: floors scrubbed and carpets beaten every Saturday, a service on the first of every month, name days celebrated for the whole district. The husband says «le mieux est l'ennemi du bien», the best is the enemy of the good, and admits: «I'm frightened. Life must go on, something may change; and nothing can be better than the present». Masha feels «that life was repeating itself», and that her love «had stopped and grew no more». And then the key sentence: «custom was daily petrifying our lives into one fixed shape… The morning always found us cheerful; we were polite at dinner, and affectionate in the evening».

This is worth pausing on. In the moonlit garden Masha felt that everything «must remain fixed for ever in its beauty». A few months later the same image returns as custom that hardens their life into «one fixed shape»; in the Russian original Tolstoy uses one verb for both, zakovat', to put in chains. **The wish of the entry came true literally, and became Death in the middle.** In this tail love does not freeze because of something bad. It freezes because two people wanted too much to hold on to something good.

The same middle shows in the roles. The romance began as a lesson: the guardian promises, «I shall put you through an examination in spring», and all her thoughts at that time were, in her words, «not mine but his thoughts and feelings». His gaze «draws out of me the very thought he wants». In Petersburg it pleased her «to find myself in these surroundings not merely his equal but his superior», and now it is she who pulls him to the balls. After the quarrel over a reception she notes: «We had changed parts». Wen writes that Death can suggest «the waning of power of one authority and the growing, ascending power of a new». What dies in the couple is the form "the elder leads, the younger learns", and for a long time nothing shows what will take its place. Among the difficulties of the thirteenth energy Lisovskaya names this one too: one partner forces the other to change. In the novella they both do it, by turns.

The bitterest line of the middle belongs to the husband: «So you make a sacrifice! Well, so do I. What could be better? We compete in generosity -- what an example of family happiness!» After it, for three years, their relations «seemed to have taken a fixed shape which could not become either better or worse». Wen calls this state, in Death reversed, a plateau: the transition is due, but nothing moves.

sections.h2: Who is to blame when Death stands in the middle
paragraphs: The whole second half of the novella is a search for the guilty one. «How am I guilty before you?» — «I am to blame». «You loved too little». — «I was to blame». Tolstoy gives the answer to the husband in the last chapter: «time is to blame for that, and we ourselves», and a little later, more honestly still: «Who is to blame, I do not know».

The numbers answer the same way. Thirteen is not in the personal tail of either partner in any couple with the 3-13-10 tail. Nobody brings Death into the middle; the two of them put it together. In about 77% of such couples it is 4 + 9: one partner's Emperor and the other's Hermit. In the remaining 23% it is 3 + 10: one partner has The Empress in the middle of the personal tail, the other has The Wheel of Fortune. **The two other cards of the tail reach the couple from two sides, and their meeting makes Death**: a house that wants «for ever» meets a wheel that turns. There is no culprit in such a sum.

The novella also offers a temptation to skip the middle. At the spa an Italian marquis who resembles the husband «by his smile and the expression of his brow» explains to a friend: «To make life a romance is the one thing worth doing. And with me romance never breaks off in the middle». It is the promise of a romance without Death. Masha nearly gives in, and that same evening takes the train to her husband. Such a romance is not on offer to a 3-13-10 couple: they always have a middle, and the only question is what the two of them carry out of it.

One more detail — a coincidence, not a clue, but hard to miss. On the day he gives himself away, Sergey Mikhaylych says of himself: «I feel like a boy of thirteen -- I want to play at horses and climb trees». After the wedding, when Masha asks him to say the prayers with her, he laughs: «It's as if I were ten years old again». Tolstoy put two numbers of the 3-13-10 tail into his mouth at moments of happiness.

sections.h2: The Wheel of Fortune: each time of life has its own love
paragraphs: A couple's main task is read mostly through the minus: what does not work and what they will have to learn. Lisovskaya's key to the Wheel is cyclicity: highs and lows replace each other, and the fight is not with the change itself but with the habit of blaming fate and each other for it. In the novella the minus of the Wheel is the last conversation on the veranda, in the spring rain.

Masha accuses: «Why did you give me a freedom for which I was unfit? Why did you stop teaching me? If you had wished it… none of all this would have happened!» Then she pleads: «Let everything be as it was before… It can be, can't it?» These are two attempts to stop the wheel: find who pushed it, and turn it back. At first he answers too smoothly: «No; I might as well wish to have wings. It is impossible». Then honestly: «I weep for that past love which can never return… Love remains, but not the old love».

The plus of the Wheel is in his own words: «Each time of life has its own kind of love». And: «Don't let us try to repeat life… Don't let us make pretences to ourselves». He explains what happened in the middle: «In that summer when I first knew you, I used to lie awake all night, thinking about you, and I made that love myself… So again, in Petersburg and abroad, in the course of horrible sleepless nights, I strove to shatter and destroy that love, which had come to torture me. I did not destroy it, but I destroyed that part of it which gave me pain. Then I grew calm; and I feel love still, but it is a different kind of love». In this speech Death and the Wheel work together: the old form is broken, while love itself has turned and stayed.

The Wheel shows in the scenery as well. The story returns to the house at Pokrovskoye: «the garden visible through the window… the very same bench over there above the dell, the same song of the nightingale by the pond, the same lilacs in full bloom, the same moon shining above the house; and yet, in everything such a terrible inconceivable change!» Masha plays the sonata quasi una fantasia again and looks round at the corner where he used to listen: «his chair, long unmoved, was still in its place». In her girlhood room there are two beds, and one of them is her own, where her elder son now sleeps. Her husband points to the younger one: «Now we must stand aside and make room -- for him».

The turn comes quietly: «Suddenly I realized clearly and calmly that the past feeling, like the past time itself, was gone beyond recall, and that it would be not only impossible but painful and uncomfortable to bring it back». Then the baby smiles, and Masha looks into her husband's eyes «with an ease and happiness which I had not felt for a long time». **The task of the Wheel is not to bring back the first summer but to recognise love in a new season.**

The numbers add a detail of their own. The Wheel of Fortune is in the personal tail of one of the partners in every couple with the 3-13-10 tail: in 77% it is that partner's own main task (the tail 21-4-10), in 23% the middle of the personal tail. That does not make this partner the teacher. The couple's Wheel is a sum: 10 + 18 in most couples, 16 + 21 or 7 + 21 in the rest. A task that one of them knows from a personal chart becomes shared in the couple and looks different.

sections.h2: Waite and Wen: the field, the scythe and the wheel
paragraphs: Of The Empress Waite writes: «A field of corn is ripening in front of her, and beyond there is a fall of water», and calls her «universal fecundity». It is the very field Masha watches on the day he gives himself away.

Of Death he recalls the old design of the card: «The scene is the field of life», living heads stick out of the grass, and a skeleton «with a great scythe is in the act of mowing it». The meaning, Waite adds, is transparent — death — «but the alternatives allocated to the symbol are change and transformation». On his own card «king and child and maiden» fall before the rider. Our reading for this couple: in the middle the three roles of the romance come to an end — the husband who, as Masha saw it, «had to be a demigod on a pedestal», the «dear child who has to be calmed down», and the «violet», as he called her when she was a girl.

Of the Wheel: «the perpetual motion of a fluidic universe and for the flux of human life». Reversed, Waite lists «Increase, abundance, superfluity». That is The Empress's vocabulary. The end of the tail speaks in the words of its beginning, and the tail closes into a ring.

Tolstoy leads the couple through all three pictures. The first confession comes at harvest. On the wedding day, walking back from the memorial service, they cross «the beaten and trampled stubble»; to one side a peasant is «ploughing a black strip which grew wider and wider», and ahead «a field of winter corn… showed black with occasional patches of green». Mown, ploughed and already sown — in one field, on one day.

Wen writes that the Wheel suggests «samsara… the endless cycle of birth and death». All three cards of the tail are in that phrase: birth (for Wen The Empress is «the card of fruition»), death and the circle. The village church in the novella is built the same way: the same voice had read «at Sonya's christening, at memorial services for my father, and at my mother's funeral»; the priest wears «a cope made of the pall that had covered my father's coffin»; and he is the one who marries Masha: «I christened you and by God's mercy have lived to marry you». The book opens in mourning for a mother and closes with a baby's smile.

sections.h2: Atmosphere and values: family around, choice within
paragraphs: The centre of the couple's matrix is the atmosphere, what lies between the two and is not on show. In 81.5% of couples with this tail the centre holds Judgement. Lisovskaya's key to the twentieth energy in a couple is kin and family: relatives, traditions, the influence of parents. The novella opens with this centre. Masha's mother once said that she «would like such a husband for me», her father joked «you should marry my Masha», and at the memorial service before the wedding Masha feels her father's blessing upon her. The young couple live in the house of his mother, where everything was set up before them. The minus of the same centre is a sharp cooling, when neither can say what they feel. In Tolstoy: «Never had he looked at me so coldly, never had he spoken to me so coldly». With a centre of 20 the couple's tail follows the same arithmetic as a personal matrix: the main task plus the centre give the entry, 10 + 20 = 30 → 3.

In 18.5% of couples the centre holds Strength. In the minus of the atmosphere Lisovskaya describes it as a struggle for leadership in which each partner has their own truth. In Tolstoy this is Masha's line, said coldly: «You are always in the right».

The couple's values are The Lovers in 71.1% of cases and The Devil in 28.9%. The Lovers here are love as a choice that is made again: Sergey Mikhaylych says «I made that love myself», and later he remade it himself. The Devil is the shadow of that choice: passion and the wish to possess. Lisovskaya's closing thought on the fifteenth energy in a couple: no one belongs to anyone. In the novella Masha reproaches her husband: «Why did you not exercise your authority?», and he explains that he «had no right to put pressure on» her. This is our reading: the value of such a union is a freedom that never had to be taken away.

sections.h2: How a couple lives this tail in its strong version
paragraphs: The strong version of the tail does not promise that Death will pass the couple by. It changes the way the two of them meet it.

ul: **Call the end of the romance the end of a form, not of the union.** A wedding, a move, the birth of a child or a new job can end the old way of being together. That is not yet the end of the couple.

**Don't keep the garden «for ever».** A home needs habits. But when feelings run to a timetable — «cheerful» in the morning, «polite» at dinner, «affectionate» in the evening — the form has outlived its content.
**Don't look for a culprit in the turn.** The sum 4 + 9 or 3 + 10 belongs to no one. "What do we need now?" is a more useful question than "Who started it?"
**Tell the stories through to the third ending.** A couple can talk about itself through «Mr A and Miss B» as long as this helps to tell the truth rather than to avoid it.
**Grieve for the past, but don't repeat it.** «I weep for that past love» and «Don't let us try to repeat life» stand side by side in the novella and do not get in each other's way.

**Open the house.** Lisovskaya advises couples with the Wheel not to shut themselves up in each other. The last scene of the novella is full of people: Katya and Sonya wet from the rain, the nurse with Vanya, laughter on the veranda.

paragraphs: Each point of a couple is the sum of the same points in the two personal matrices, reduced to 22. The couple's middle is not derived from the two outer numbers: it is added up from the personal middles.

The partner born on 11.02.1976 has the personal tail 9-9-18, the partner born on 14.10.1975 has 21-4-10. This is the most common combination for the couple tail 3-13-10: 77% of such couples are formed this way. In the rest, one partner has the tail 21-10-16 (19%) or 21-10-7 (4%), and the other has 9-3-21.

The example shows the whole story of the numbers. The Wheel is the second partner's personal main task. The couple's centre is 9 + 11 = 20, Judgement; the couple's values are 6, The Lovers. Point H of the couple's matrix also holds 10, and the reading marks The Wheel of Fortune as a card that appears both in the tail and at an additional point: in the couple method this reinforces the theme of the section. This happens in about 16% of couples with this tail. The Empress from point M appears twice in the reading: in the tail and in the sphere «Relationship and common language», where she is labelled «Common language».

intro: About one couple in 227 has this tail. Literature has an exact double for it: a novella by Tolstoy whose last page says «That day ended the romance of our marriage» and calls it the beginning of happiness.

faq.q: Does Death in a couple's 3-13-10 tail mean a break-up?
faq.a: No. Numbers do not predict events. Death in the middle of a couple's tail speaks of a change of form: the first way of loving each other ends, and with it roles, habits and expectations. The union goes on, as long as the couple does not mistake the end of the romance for the end of the relationship.

faq.q: How is the couple tail 3-13-10 different from the personal tail 3-13-10?
faq.a: It is a different calculation with different roles for the points. The personal tail 3-13-10 occurs for 149 dates since 1900 and describes the task of one person; the site has a separate article about it. A couple's tail is added up from two personal matrices and describes the shared task of two people: the entry is what the couple wants together, the middle is how it travels, the main task is what it has to learn.

faq.q: Why is the middle 13 if 3 + 10 also make 13?
faq.a: A coincidence of arithmetic. The couple's middle is the sum of the partners' personal middles: 4 + 9 in 77% of such couples and 3 + 10 in 23%. It is not recalculated from the outer numbers of the couple's tail, even though here the result happens to be the same.

faq.q: Are there couple tails with the same numbers in a different order?
faq.a: No. The entry of a couple's tail is always a multiple of three, so 10 and 13 never come first, and the order 3-10-13 does not occur for any couple. Of these three numbers only the tail 3-13-10 is possible for a couple.

faq.q: How rare is the couple tail 3-13-10?
faq.a: It occurs in about one couple in 227, which is 0.44% of all couples, and ranks 60th of the 97 possible couple tails.

report: Tolstoy wrote a novella about a couple in which the wedding stands exactly in the middle of the book, and the last sentence sounds like a verdict but turns out to be a promise: «That day ended the romance of our marriage». The 3-13-10 tail is built the same way. The Empress at the entry, Death in the middle and the Wheel of Fortune in the main task tell not of a break-up, but of how the romance ends halfway through a shared life while the union goes on.

report.h3: A garden that does not want seasons

report: The entry to the task is what the couple wants together. For The Empress this is a house where there is plenty of everything and everything grows. In Family Happiness this entry is written down almost word for word. Sergey Mikhaylych's dream is «A quiet secluded life in the country», then work, rest, nature, books, music, love for one's neighbour. Masha answers that this is all she has ever wanted. The first, unintended confession comes during the harvest, when before her eyes summer turns «into autumn».

Yet on the very first summer evening on the veranda he says: «I wish I could spend all my life here, sitting in this veranda». A moment later he adds: «life won't sit still». The tail's main task is spoken aloud before the love has even begun.

The resistance of the entry hides in two words: «for ever». In the moonlit garden Masha feels «that the whole scene must remain fixed for ever in its beauty». **The minus of this entry is the wish for a garden without seasons.**

Such a couple also has a common language of its own: the two talk about themselves as if about other people. Sergey Mikhaylych declares himself through the story of Mr A and Miss B, which has «two different endings», and Masha invents a third and makes her own confession through it. A tale told in the third person helps to tell the truth, until it starts helping to avoid it. Later Masha will note: «conversation flowed more easily in the presence of a third person».

report.h3: A wish that came true literally

report: A few months after the wedding the same image returns. Now it is custom that is «daily petrifying our lives into one fixed shape… The morning always found us cheerful; we were polite at dinner, and affectionate in the evening». **The wish of the entry came true literally, and became Death in the middle.** In this tail love freezes not because of something bad, but because two people wanted too much to hold on to something good.

Waite describes Death as a change of form: what ends is not life but the mask it has worn until now. What ends in the couple is the form in which the romance lived: one leads, the other learns. At first Masha's thoughts were «not mine but his thoughts and feelings»; later «We had changed parts». The bitterest line of the middle belongs to the husband: «We compete in generosity -- what an example of family happiness!»

There is also a temptation to skip the middle. A marquis at the spa promises a romance that «never breaks off in the middle». Such a romance is not on offer to a 3-13-10 couple: they always have a middle, and the only question is what the two of them carry out of it.

report.h3: No culprit, even in the numbers

report: The second half of the novella is a search for the guilty one: she asks how she is guilty before him, she tells him he loved too little, he answers «I was to blame». The answer comes in the last chapter: «time is to blame for that, and we ourselves», and then, more honestly still: «Who is to blame, I do not know».

The numbers answer the same way. The thirteenth card is not in the personal tail of either partner: nobody brings Death into the middle, only the couple puts it together. Sometimes it is made, quite literally, of the other two cards of the tail: one partner has The Empress in the middle of the personal tail, the other has the Wheel. A house that wants «for ever» meets a wheel that turns.

report.h3: Each time of life has its own love

report: The main task is read through the minus. The minus of the Wheel is two attempts to stop the turn: find who pushed it, and bring everything back. «Let everything be as it was before… It can be, can't it?» Masha pleads.

The plus of the Wheel is spoken in reply: «Each time of life has its own kind of love» and «Don't let us try to repeat life». Sergey Mikhaylych admits that he destroyed not love but only «that part of it which gave me pain», and «I feel love still, but it is a different kind of love». And straight away, honestly: «I weep for that past love». Grieving for the past is allowed; repeating it is not.

The Wheel shows in the scenery too: the same garden, the same bench above the dell, the same nightingale and the same moon above the house, «and yet, in everything such a terrible inconceivable change!» Masha's girlhood bed now holds her son. Reversed, the Wheel in Waite's list means increase, abundance, superfluity: The Empress's vocabulary, so the end of the tail speaks in the words of its beginning.

**The task of the Wheel is not to bring back the first summer but to recognise love in a new season.** The strong version of this tail does not skip Death in the middle. It calls the end of the romance the end of a form, not of the union, looks for no culprit in the turn, and opens the house to people, children and shared work. Tolstoy's novella ends exactly this way: the romance is over, and «a new life and a quite different happiness» has only just been founded.
